---
title: "Write a report you can defend"
---

## Create a draft without overwriting your writing

Run the dataset's `create_report.R` command. It creates a draft in ignored
`reports/` and keeps an existing draft unchanged. The report is independent
of the book; you do not add it to `_quarto.yml`.

Edit the prompts into your own account of the question, inputs, decisions,
results, checks, limitations and next scientific action. Keep your report
short: use the most informative figures in the narrative and link the rest
as supporting evidence.

## Every claim needs a location

For a diversity claim, name the metric, groups, summary and source table.
For a community test, record the distance, transformation, model, permutations,
R-squared, p-value and dispersion result. For an OTU association, give its ID,
tested contrast, natural-log effect, uncertainty, BH-adjusted p-value and
pseudo-count sensitivity result. Do not silently substitute a genus name for
an OTU-level finding.

Distinguish a descriptive difference from an adjusted association and from a
causal claim. Adjustment addresses only the measured variables in that model.

## Render separately

From the project root:

```bash
cd reports
quarto render zackular-report.qmd --to html
cd ..
```

Use `synthetic-report.qmd` or `my-study-report.qmd` for the other examples.
Check that images load, numerical claims match the current complete run,
and all placeholder text has been replaced. New outputs do not update your
written interpretations automatically.

## Record AI's contribution

State the tool/model if known, date, task, what you supplied, what you adopted
and how you checked it. First write your own observation; ask AI to challenge
it using actual tables; make the final revision yourself. Do not share
identifying or restricted participant information.
